classification.difficultyReason: Apply the complement of A to single, overlapping, disjoint and nested sets.

content.prompt: On each diagram, shade the region $A'$.

spec.description: Single circle A in a rectangle; A is labelled outside its circle and inside the rectangle.

answer.short: Shade everything in the rectangle outside $A$.
answer.worked: $A'$ contains the elements of the universal set that are not in $A$. Leave the circle white and shade the surrounding region.

spec.description: Light orange outside A; A remains white.
Overlapping circles A and B in the universal rectangle.
spec.mathematics: Complement of A when A and B overlap.

answer.short: Shade everything outside $A$, including the $B$-only region.
answer.worked: $A'$ excludes all of $A$, including the overlap. Shade the $B$-only region and the region outside both circles.

spec.description: Everything outside A is light orange, including B only.
Two disjoint circles A and B in the universal rectangle.

answer.short: Shade everything outside $A$, including all of $B$.
answer.worked: The circles are disjoint, so all of $B$ is outside $A$. Shade $B$ and the region outside both circles; leave $A$ white.

spec.description: Everything outside A, including all of B, is light orange.
Large oval B contains a smaller oval A towards its lower right.
spec.mathematics: A is a proper subset of B.

answer.short: Shade everything outside the smaller oval $A$.
answer.worked: $A'$ includes the part of $B$ outside $A$ and the region outside $B$. Leave only the smaller oval $A$ white.

spec.description: Everything outside the smaller oval A is light orange.
spec.mathematics: Universal set minus A, with A contained in B.
